papers.title: Tensile and fatigue behaviors of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V: Influence of surface texture and removal
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Auburn University, Auburn, AL 36849, USA

corresponding_authors.name: Nima Shamsaei
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Auburn University, Auburn, AL 36849, USA

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的拉伸与疲劳行为，重点关注表面纹理及其去除的影响，完全符合L1层的力学与疲劳性能要求。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover post-processing treatments (e.g., HIP, heat treatment) or femoral stem applications, but it is fully within the L1 scope.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的表面纹理及去除对其拉伸和疲劳性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过改变表面纹理状态（如机加工去除）进行拉伸和疲劳实验。
summary_zh.result: 表面纹理显著影响疲劳寿命，去除表面粗糙度可大幅提升疲劳性能。
summary_zh.validation: 通过对比不同表面状态下的力学测试结果进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the influence of surface texture and its removal on the tensile and fatigue behaviors of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Tensile and fatigue experiments were conducted on specimens with different surface conditions, including as-built and machined surfaces.
summary_en.result: Surface texture significantly affects fatigue life; removing surface roughness substantially improves fatigue performance.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through mechanical testing and comparison of different surface states.

papers.title: Gradient structural disorder induces isotropic and high-energy-absorbing behavior in porous Ti-6Al-4V Alloy
papers.abstract: • Gradient disorder boosts energy absorption up to 600 % along the y-axis. • Anisotropy in modulus and absorption reduced by 96 % and 93 %, respectively. • Trapezo-rhombic cells fabricated via L-PBF improve stress distribution. • FEA and experiments confirm enhanced isotropy and deformation uniformity. • Optimized disorder gradient enables multifunctional energy-absorbing design. Porous Ti-6Al-4V alloys, renowned for their lightweight nature and exceptional energy-absorption capabilities, hold great promise for aerospace and biomedical applications. However, their widespread adoption has been limited by challenges such as mechanical anisotropy and localized stress concentrations. In this study, we propose novel gradient-disordered porous architectures fabricated via advanced laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) to overcome these issues. Trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron cells were employed as the basic structural unit, and gradient-disordered layers (1–4) were strategically integrated to improve mechanical performance through controlled heterogeneity. Experimental results revealed that the gradient-disordered designs significantly enhanced energy absorption, achieving increases of up to 600% along the y -axis and 300% along the x -axis compared with ordered structures. Furthermore, these architectures reduced anisotropy in normalized Young’s modulus and energy absorption by 96% and 93%, respectively, resulting in nearly isotropic behavior. Compression tests and finite element simulations confirmed improved isotropy, suppression of shear band development, and more uniform stress distribution, underscoring the robustness of the proposed designs. Overall, these findings highlight gradient-disordered porous architectures as a promising strategy for optimizing porous Ti-6Al-4V alloys, particularly in aerospace and biomedical applications requiring high energy absorption, isotropy, and durability.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究了LPBF制备的多孔Ti-6Al-4V合金的力学性能，包括能量吸收和各向异性，属于L1方向核心内容。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on porous structures rather than solid mechanical characterization, but it still provides experimental mechanical data for Ti-6Al-4V AM, which is within scope; no fatigue testing is performed.

summary_zh.motivation: 克服多孔Ti-6Al-4V各向异性和应力集中问题。
summary_zh.method: 设计梯度无序结构并采用L-PBF制备，结合压缩实验和有限元模拟。
summary_zh.result: 梯度无序结构使能量吸收提升600%，各向异性降低96%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过压缩实验和FEA验证了力学性能改善。

summary_en.motivation: To overcome mechanical anisotropy and stress concentration in porous Ti-6Al-4V alloys for enhanced energy absorption.
summary_en.method: Gradient-disordered porous architectures based on trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron cells were designed and fabricated via laser powder bed fusion, then characterized by compression tests and finite element simulations.
summary_en.result: The gradient-disordered designs achieved up to 600% increase in energy absorption and reduced anisotropy in modulus and absorption by 96% and 93%, respectively, resulting in nearly isotropic behavior.
summary_en.validation: Experimental compression tests and finite element simulations confirmed improved isotropy, suppressed shear bands, and uniform stress distribution.
